# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
FROM THE NIGHT, five instances of one shape, which is why it is written as a shape rather
than as five bugs. A CONTROL REPORTS HEALTHY ABOUT A PROPERTY IT NEVER EXAMINED.

  1. scripts/doctor.py proved fence liveness inside a throwaway project it built itself,
     where the schema gap that actually broke the fence cannot arise. It printed PASS
     while one writer per file was enforced NOWHERE in the repository, for every session.
  2. scripts/migrate_install.py asked whether a hook was WIRED. Wiring was intact and the
     code behind it was hundreds of commits stale, so it printed NOTHING TO DO about the
     same broken install. This is the round being briefed.
  3. The write site inventory could not see sixteen of its own sites, and a third blind
     spot after that: json.dump(obj, fh) has never been matched by ANY generation of the
     patterns. All three were found by whoever happened to be working inside it, never by
     an audit of it.
  4. M14 was RETIRED against a hook nobody named. The probes ran against the repaired
     installed copy and returned zero warnings, but M14 names a different hook, so "did
     not reproduce" was measured against the wrong subject. The pack then repeated it as
     settled. M14 is open again.
  5. An audit of the backlog's own done markers found ONE ITEM IN FOURTEEN marked done
     that was not done, and no control found any of them.

FROM THE SESSION THAT WROTE THIS PACK, in the order they happened.

  A GATE STARTED ON ANOTHER SESSION'S TREE. Asked to prepare a restart, this session began
  a full gate at 00:47 to certify a starting point, without first checking whether anyone
  was working. The night session was mid commit. Worse than a wasted run: the battery
  fence would then have refused that session's OWN lane for the whole 8 to 19 minutes.
  Aborted within a minute by killing the gate by PID after printing the target, and the
  sentinel was cleared so no one could read the aborted run as a verdict. CHECK FOR
  WRITERS BEFORE STARTING A GATE, not only before writing.

  A COMPLETION CLAIMED AS FINAL WAS NOT FINAL. At 03:23 this session read a close pack and
  reported the night closed with nothing remaining. The night then landed five more
  commits and rewrote its own pack twice. A close pack existing does not mean a session
  has stopped, and "closed" is not a stable state while budget and clock remain.

  A COMMAND NAMED THE WRONG TOOL. `handover-ack` is a bm_store command; this session ran
  it against bm_handover eleven times and got eleven unknown-command errors before
  reading the tool list. The clearing command detect prints names its own path. Read it.

STANDING, AND EACH COST SOMETHING ONCE.

  READ EXIT CODES DIRECTLY, NEVER THROUGH A PIPE. `cmd | tail -2 && git push` pushed a red
  suite to main, because a pipeline's status is the LAST command's.
  NEVER TRUST pgrep -f ALONE. It matched a session's own shell twice in one night.
  A DENY IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF ANY FENCE TEST. The hook fails open by design.
  READ THE REASON, NOT ONLY THE VERDICT. Two fences guard the same write; the cheaper one
  answers first, and a denial during a gate is the battery fence, not ownership.
  SURFACE THE PRIOR DECISION WHEN YOU ASK. The founder was asked whether to push the
  v3.3.2 tag without being shown that his own board recorded a decision to hold it.
